releases.notes:
- New: a **Terminal** panel at the bottom of the window, as in VS Code. Run your AI agents and the nexus command there while the task views above update by themselves. Open or hide it from any page with the terminal button in the header, with Ctrl+ (⌘+ on a Mac — the key left of 1), or from the tray icon's *Open Terminal*; drag its top edge to resize it.
- Terminals open in tabs (+ for a new one, Ctrl+Shift+T / ⌘T), start in a default folder you choose in Settings → CLI & Agents → Terminal (your home folder if none), and use your usual shell unless you set another there. Hiding the panel, or going to the Widget Builder and back, keeps them running with their output.
- In the installed app, nexus always works in the Terminal panel, even where it is not on your PATH (for example the AppImage). Links printed in the terminal open in your browser; copy / paste with Ctrl+Shift+C / V (⌘C / ⌘V on a Mac).
- New: nexus ui lets you (or your AI agent) drive the app window from the command line, without changing any data: nexus ui open-task TASK-00012 (or a nexus://task/… link) shows a task, nexus ui new-task --title … --set priority=High opens the new-task form filled in for you to check and save, nexus ui view calendar switches view, nexus ui calendar 2026-12-04 --scope week jumps the Calendar to a day, week or month, and nexus ui tab --filter "status=In Progress" --not priority=Low --due this-month opens a new tab with live filters. nexus ui status tells what the window shows. Folders with read-only access may use them too.
- New agent skill nexus-ui (Settings → CLI & Agents → Agent skills) that teaches agents these commands.

0.7.5:
- Fix: when config.json is being rewritten by another program at the moment Nexus reads it (more likely on a busy computer), Nexus now waits for the write to finish instead of taking the file for empty, so the profile list is never read as empty by mistake. A config.json that is really broken is still detected after a short wait, and does not slow Nexus down again until it changes.

0.7.4:
- Journal: a day without a debrief can now get its timesheet straight from the app. *Create a timesheet* (in the Journal view's empty day, next to a day's briefing, or in the Calendar's popup of a day with only a briefing) opens the timesheet rows alone; *Create* saves them as that day's debrief, from the source nexus.
- New nexus journal update <day> <file>: changes an existing journal entry with only the parts given (summary, notices, sections by id; "remove": true deletes a section) and never creates one, so an agent can complete the timesheet you started in the app without replacing it.
- New nexus journal create <day> [file]: creates the debrief of a day that has none (an empty timesheet, or a document); refused when the day already has a debrief.
- nexus journal import now warns when it adds a second debrief to a day, since the hours of both are counted.
- The nexus-journal agent skill checks for an existing debrief of the day and updates it instead of importing a new one.

0.7.3:
- Calendar: a completed routine no longer counts as active. The ↻ number on a day counts only the routines still to do; the completed ones stay in the day's list, at the bottom, greyed and marked "done". A day whose routines are all completed shows a grey ✓ without a number.
- Journal: a briefing's and a debrief's sections are now tabs (the first one open), in the Journal view and in the Calendar's popup; the debrief's *Nexus activity* is its last tab. The source's notes (missing mail, warnings) are folded behind a "N notes from the source" toggle, closed by default.
- Journal: when editing a debrief, the activity of a timesheet row is picked by typing, like the pick lists of the task sheet.
- Journal: the Calendar's briefing / debrief popup is larger, and your own note on a briefing or a debrief can now be added and changed right there.

0.7.2:
- New **Journal**: a morning **briefing** and an end-of-day **debrief** for each day, sent by your AI agents (with access to your calendar, mail or other tools) in Nexus's own nexus-journal/1 format. Nexus shows what they say and links it to your tasks by id; hours, meetings and mail stay in the Journal, never in the tasks.
- The Calendar marks the days that have them: ☀ *Briefing* and ☾ the hours of the debrief on each day (a dot and the hours in the month grid). A click opens the day's popup with the summary, the agenda, the tasks to tackle with the agent's advice, the timesheet.
- New **Journal** view (Views → Journal): a day's briefing and debrief side by side, what Nexus itself saw that day (tasks created, completed, commented), and per week or month the hours you worked by activity, by task or by day, with CSV export. A mini calendar marks the days with entries. Files can also be imported from there.
- A debrief can be corrected: its summary and each timesheet row (activity, description, linked tasks, hours), rows added or removed, and *Restore original*. A new import from the agent never overwrites your corrections: it waits until you choose *Use the new one* or *Keep mine*. Every entry can also take your own note.
- The task sheet lists the days the task appears in the Journal, with the hours logged on it.
- New Settings → Journal: what timesheet hours are booked on — task fields chained, up to three (by default Project › Section, picked from a list of their values), or free text —; today's briefing in a popup when Nexus opens (off by default); the sources the entries came from (rename, delete their entries).
- Settings now lists its sections in a menu on the left.
- New nexus journal commands: import, list, get, timesheet (hours by activity, task or day; --csv), activities, edit, restore, pending, note, delete, sources, source-rename, source-delete, schema (the format as a JSON Schema).
- New agent skill **nexus-journal** (Settings → CLI & Agents → Agent skills): how an agent writes and sends a briefing or a debrief, and reads the hours back.

0.7.1:
- Fixed: your list of profiles could disappear if Nexus read its settings file (config.json) at the very moment another program was writing it, or if the file was damaged. Nexus now reads it again, never overwrites a file it cannot read, and keeps a damaged one aside as config.json.unreadable-… instead of losing it.

0.7.0:
- Your data is now encrypted: every database and backup is encrypted with one key, kept by your computer's keychain. Without it nobody can read your tasks, not even from a backup in Dropbox, OneDrive, iCloud or on Google Drive.
- The first start after updating asks you to set it up and shows your recovery code: keep it, it opens your backups on a new computer or after reinstalling the system. You confirm it by typing its highlighted group back. Your profiles are encrypted right away, tasks included.
- On a computer without a keychain (Linux without a Secret Service), Nexus asks for a startup password instead, each time it starts; the recovery code resets it if you forget it.
- Already use Nexus on another computer? Choose "I already use Nexus on another computer", pick the backup folder and type that computer's recovery code: both computers then share the same key and open each other's backups.
- New Settings → Profiles → Encryption: how your key is kept, and a new recovery code when you need one.
- Backups are now encrypted too (named ….enc.db). Old backups in your backup folder stay as they are, marked "not encrypted", with a button to delete them; on Google Drive the old ones are deleted once the first encrypted backup is there.
- The nexus command works on the encrypted data through the app; while Nexus waits for its password it answers that Nexus is locked.
- Two computers that each set up their own key can now share backups: when you restore or load a backup made on the other computer, Nexus asks for that computer's recovery code, then either unifies the keys (this computer switches to the other key, its own older backups still open, and one recovery code is left for both) or restores only that backup. Importing a database file from the other computer works the same way.
- Computers with different keys no longer overwrite each other's key file in a shared backup folder: each key has its own nexus-vault-<keyId>.json.
- Settings → CLI & Agents → Access now lets you choose the profile each approved folder works on, and Settings → Profiles shows which folders use nexus on each profile.
- Settings is reorganized: General Settings (formerly Appearance, now also with *Start Nexus when you log in* under Startup), Profiles, Customization (formerly Fields), CLI & Agents, Data, About.

0.6.5:
- The nexus command now works through the app: it never opens your databases itself. Each folder needs your approval once: run nexus auth request there and allow it in the app (read only, or read and write). The token is saved in .nexus/ in that folder; nexus auth status shows what it may do and nexus auth logout gives the access up.
- Each approved folder works on one profile. Deleting and changing many tasks at once can be refused, confirmed by you in a dialog each time, or approved on their own with full access for a few hours (within limits you set, after a snapshot).
- New Settings → CLI & Agents → Access: the folders that can use nexus, their access level, full access and its limits, revoking, and the latest requests.
- Profiles, imports, restores, the backup folder and schedule, Google Drive and field setup are now done in the app only; nexus refuses them and says so. Reading the setup (nexus field required, nexus snapshot config, …) still works.
- Nexus starts at login in the background (tray only), so nexus always finds it; you can turn this off in Settings → CLI & Agents → Access. When the app is not running, the installed nexus command starts it.
- Files stay on your side: nexus reads the files you give it and writes the ones you ask for (export --out, attachment save) itself.
- The agent skills explain how to get access and where to do in the app what nexus no longer does.

- Command line: nexus desk now changes the Desktop as the app does. place / return take tasks out onto the desk and send them back, note adds, edits and removes sticky notes (and sets their font), routines shows or hides the routines board, and new starts a new desk. Without a position, things go where nothing lies, in view.

- Routines: new schedules: working days, weekend days, chosen days of the week, and monthly every N months. Each occurrence is created once; one left open becomes overdue and the Calendar lists it under Overdue.
- Task List → Actions → Edit Selected…: change many tasks at once in the task sheet, with only the fields they share; an eraser empties a field on every selected task; changes are confirmed and applied together. CLI: nexus task bulk-update.
- Fix: a group's header checkbox selects that group's tasks only.

- Routines are created and edited in the task sheet: a routine block (schedule, dates, steps) under the title replaces the separate routine dialog.
- Task sheet: a note's edit box opens as tall as the note and grows while typing, up to half the pane.
- Fixes: a highlighted value in a pick list stays on one line; "Unsaved changes" no longer shows when nothing changed.

- Calendar: today's open routines are listed with the day's tasks (Today / Week and the month cell), outlined in green; a click opens the routine.
- Pick-list search ranks the best matches first and shows the matching words in bold.

- Google Drive backups per profile: snapshots go to the profile's own Drive folder (no Drive desktop app needed), with restore, download and the newer-backup check at startup. CLI: nexus snapshot drive.
- New profiles can start from a copy of an existing Nexus database file (checked, then copied); each profile needs its own backup folder.
- Task List: folded groups are remembered, each group has its own "+ New Task" pre-filled with the group's value, and a new task starts with the values of single-value filters.
- Completed tasks are hidden in the list and the kanban unless "Show completed" is on or a filter asks for them.
- Pick lists of more than three values filter as you type.
- Desktop: a Projects popup chooses which projects lie on the desk (filter, All / None / Only these). CLI: nexus desk projects.
- Monthly routines can start on a day of the month ("every month from the 15th").
- Profiles: pick the icon from the icon popup. File dialogs open on the app window.
- Links in descriptions, notes and resources open in the system browser (mailto: in the mail app) instead of replacing the app window; nexus://task links open the task in Nexus.

- Routines: checklists that come back every day, weekday, Monday, week or month. Each period creates a task with one sub-task per step, kept as the routine's history; a Routines view lists open occurrences and routines (pause, resume, end, history), the Calendar shows each day's routines and the Desktop can show a routines board with tickable steps. CLI: nexus routine.
- Settings are split into tabs and sub-tabs (Appearance, Fields, Profiles, Data, CLI & Agents, About), and remember the last one per profile.
- Settings → CLI & Agents downloads the agent skills for the nexus CLI as a zip.
- Date inputs get Today / Tomorrow / Next week buttons; the due date is a date only; new custom field types Date and Date and time.
- Desktop: ten note colours, one font for all notes, deleting a note asks first; Add a task skips completed tasks while they are hidden; a task sent back no longer brings its put-away folder out.
- Calendar: each day's tasks (Today, Week and the Month grid, "+N more" list included) are ordered by priority, highest first; tasks without a priority come last. Overdue stays sorted by due date.
- Calendar: the Calendar item of the Views list shows how many open tasks are overdue or due today (hidden at zero).

- Tasks in a list, kanban, calendar and dashboard (with a custom widget builder); projects and sections; dimensions, custom fields and contacts; filterable and required fields; task sub-tabs, Favorites and a Desktop view to lay tasks out; a two-column task sheet with in-place editing and Duplicate.
- Data stays in a local SQLite database per profile; only immutable snapshots go to Dropbox / OneDrive / iCloud folders, and a newer backup on another device is offered at startup.
- The nexus command line drives the same databases as the app, with installable agent skills for AI assistants.
